qualification: bounded local early-boot measurement; not userspace, workload, hardware, or release qualification

fixture.commandLine: console=ttyS0 rdinit=/init panic=-1 plus a unique runner-owned dory.pvh_run_id

method.description: Six fresh runner processes used the same verified inputs, release binary, limits, and requested workloads. Three tier-one-enabled runs were followed by three disabled controls; every run deliberately stopped at exactly 100,000,000 retired instructions.

verification.measuredHighCanonicalMemoryCMOV: passed against the interpreter for true and false predicates
verification.completeMeasuredDelayTSCBody: all nine instructions passed against the interpreter for both conditional-memory paths
verification.dbtAndPCGate: 1,427 tests in 171 suites passed; one pinned PVH environment test skipped because its environment variables were absent
verification.enabledStateAndCounterStability: All three enabled trials reported byte-for-byte identical architectural state, execution statistics, and JIT counters.

interpretation: Admitting the measured scalar-load and memory-CMOV delay_tsc body moves 99.916% of this bounded run's instructions into native blocks and improves median throughput by 7.17x over the unchanged tier-one-disabled control. The result measures the complete current tier-one path, not the memory-CMOV change in isolation.
limitations: Every run intentionally exhausted its 100,000,000-instruction budget before console output or userspace; no requested guest workload ran and no boot-success claim is made.

The tier-one-enabled endpoint differs from the older pre-memory-CMOV enabled series and from the disabled control because each instruction-budget sample stops wherever its execution path reaches that boundary; the exact measured block has separate interpreter-differential semantic coverage.
KASLR remained enabled, so disabled runs did not have identical terminal registers or RIPs; they are timing controls, not a cross-setting architectural-equivalence oracle.
Three samples per setting on one Apple M2 Pro do not establish a cross-host confidence interval or any G1-G5 release target.
Raw run receipts remain in an ignored local build directory and are not release evidence.
